# prime-selectbutton

prime-rs: SelectButton component (PrimeNG port)

[Live demo](https://anton-avramchuk.github.io/prime-rs/selectbutton) · [API docs](https://docs.rs/prime-selectbutton) · [Port notes](https://github.com/anton-avramchuk/prime-rs/blob/HEAD/docs/selectbutton.md)

SelectButton — port of `p-selectbutton` from PrimeNG 21.1.10.

Markup and classes as in PrimeNG: root `div.p-selectbutton[role=group]` (instead of the `<p-selectbutton>` host), inside a
`ToggleButton` per option with `on_label = off_label = label`.

Single selection is a two-way signal `value: RwSignal<Option<String>>`, multiple selection (`multiple`) is
`values: RwSignal<Vec<String>>`. Without a signal the component keeps internal state (`default_value`, `default_values`).

```rust
use leptos::prelude::*;
use prime_selectbutton::{SelectButton, SelectButtonOption};

let value = RwSignal::new(Some("one-way".to_owned()));
let options = vec![SelectButtonOption::new("One-Way", "one-way"), SelectButtonOption::new("Return", "return")];
let html = view! { <SelectButton options=options value=value /> }.to_html();
assert!(html.contains("p-selectbutton") && html.contains("One-Way") && html.contains(r#"aria-pressed="true""#));
```

## Installation

```toml
[dependencies]
prime-selectbutton = "0.1"
prime-theme = { version = "0.1", features = ["selectbutton"] }
```

The component renders PrimeNG classes; its styles come from `prime-theme` (the Aura theme), one feature per component.
For server rendering enable the `ssr` feature in the server build and `hydrate` in the browser build.
Setting up an application (theme, SSR and hydration): https://anton-avramchuk.github.io/prime-rs/install
